name: Bofi
world_status: statement found in a copy already on file

earlier_scan.source_named: Monino, Yves. 1995. Le proto-gbaya: essai de linguistique comparative sur vingt et une langues d'Afrique centrale (Peeters) — includes Bofi phonological data; not readable online.

new_statements.quote: c) le MR s'amalgame au deuxième terme, et le schème de celui-ci est modifié ou non en fonction de la dernière more tonale du premier : 'bofi. d) pas de MR, aucune modification tonale morphologique : bangando. [...] Remarque 2. A la question, soulevée par Jacqueline THOMAS, de savoir si les différences de traitement tonal en fonction du type syllabique ne pourraient s'expliquer par la présence d'un accent dans les langues concernées, on doit répondre négativement : aucune ne présente actuellement de phénomène d'accent, d'intensité ni de longueur. L'hypothèse sera reposée en diachronie, lors de l'interprétation des correspondances phoniques (p. 345).
new_statements.translation: c) the relational morpheme (MR) merges with the second term, whose tone pattern is modified or not depending on the last tonal mora of the first: 'Bofi. d) no MR, no morphological tonal modification: Bangando. [...] Remark 2. To the question, raised by Jacqueline Thomas, whether the differences in tonal treatment according to syllable type might be explained by the presence of an accent in the languages concerned, the answer must be negative: none of them at present shows any phenomenon of accent, intensity (stress) or length. The hypothesis will be raised again diachronically, in the interpretation of the sound correspondences (p. 345).
new_statements.citation: Moñino, Yves. 1995. Le proto-gbaya: essai de linguistique comparative historique sur vingt-et-une langues d'Afrique centrale (SELAF 357; Langues et cultures africaines 20). Paris/Louvain: Peeters.
new_statements.locator: ch. 'Récapitulation contrastive', p. 285 (area c) 'bofi + Remarque 2); cross-reference p. 345 Remarque; Bofi fieldwork pp. 51-52; Bofi tones p. 405 (snippet)
new_statements.reading: no word stress according to the source
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bofi, like all 21 Gbaya languages Moñino surveyed from his own field data, has no accent/stress (nor contrastive length); word prosody is tonal (Bofi has three contrastive level tones, p. 405), with grammatical tone alternations conditioned by syllable structure and the tonal morae of adjacent words.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None mentioned (no stress at all per source).
new_statements.exceptions: None; p. 345 only entertains an accent for a pre-proto-Gbaya stage, explicitly not for the modern languages.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement is about the languages as wholes (word-level accent/intensity/length absent); made in the contrastive summary chapter covering all 21 languages, with 'bofi named on the same page. The Bofi-specific chapter (pp. 242-253) was not readable beyond snippets; the in-volume search shows it never uses the word 'accent'.
new_statements.identity_note: Moñino's 'bofi = Bofi [bff], bofi1238: spoken around Boda, préfecture de la Lobaye, CAR (p. 242 snippet), informants from Keli 2 (p. 52); same variety as the Glottolog languoid. The deciding sentence is a blanket statement over all 21 Gbaya languages in the contrastive summary chapter, with 'bofi named on the same page, not a sentence inside the Bofi chapter.

sources.note: p. 285 names 'bofi as tonal-modification area c) and Remarque 2 directly below states that none of the 21 languages (Bofi included) has any phenomenon of accent, intensity or length; p. 345 repeats 'l'absence d'accent dans les langues actuelles'; search-within-volume shows 'accent' occurs nowhere in the Bofi chapter (pp. 242-253); p. 405 snippet: 'le 'bofi possède trois tons ponctuels pertinents' (three level tones). Bofi data are Moñino's own fieldwork (530 terms, 150 sentences, informants from Keli 2, pp. 51-52).
